headline: Foreign Investors as Strength: Strategic Monitoring Can Continue, Investment Prospects Can Be Assessed
summary: Indian equities face concerns over heavy foreign institutional investor selling, geopolitical tensions, and inflation that rising crude oil prices may cause. The article notes that positive changes are now visible in the market.
why: Foreign institutional investors are large holders and traders of Indian shares, so their flows can shift the direction of the broader market. India is a major oil importer, so crude prices feed into its inflation and corporate costs.
